column11: 69,120 women in the United States were estimated to be diagnosed with endometrial cancer in 2025 (SEER). Roughly a quarter of endometrial cancer presents at stage III or IV, and about a sixth of the early-stage majority later recurs, which gives about 26,000 US patients a year with primary advanced or recurrent disease. Jemperli cost Medicare $80,337 a beneficiary on Part B in 2024, which pays average sale price. 70% of that population at that cost is $1.46bn in the US, and the US was 75% of Jemperli in 2025 (GBP 647m of GBP 861m, GSK's full-year 2025 results (6-K 0001654954-26-000892, filed 2026-02-04)), so GBP 1,440m worldwide
column12: this ceiling covers endometrial cancer and nothing else, so it binds early and the growth the filing states runs for about a year before it does. That is the point: on this arithmetic Jemperli already reaches about 40% of the US advanced or recurrent endometrial population, and RUBY made it standard of care with chemotherapy whatever the mismatch repair status, so the endometrial opportunity is most of the way filled. Its rectal cancer and other mismatch-repair-deficient solid tumour indications are real and are not in this number, and cannot all be sized from what is on file. The rectal cancer indication is now on file as a catalyst: a PDUFA of February 2027, sized at about GBP 144m a year on 2,270 US patients, and deliberately outside this ceiling until it is approved. Treat the ceiling as the endometrial franchise and those indications as upside the model does not carry
